recycling.text: The Town of Pembroke is committed to recycling and has made it easier for residents to dispose of items properly. Our collection truck has two compartments one for trash and one for recyclables. Using the Single Stream method, multiple items can be put in the curbside recycle cart. The brochure here shows what is and is not acceptable. Please take time to look this over. For further information on rules for disposal of none recyclables please see the Town Code Chapter 133. Bring to the Transfer Station for Recycling These additional items are recyclable but not allowed in the recycle cart include Electronics (TV s, Computers, Stereo systems, etc.) Printer cartridges (laser or ink jet), Rechargeable batteries, Button Cell Batteries, Alkaline, Zinc and Lithium Batteries, Auto waste (used oil, antifreeze, batteries) Fluorescent bulbs, Cell phones, Scrap metal, Appliances, Propane tanks and more. Please bring them to the Transfer Station on Tuesdays or Saturdays. Recycling Tips Please place your carts curbside by 6:45 am on the day of collection and not earlier that the previous evening Carts are not to be left curbside overnight after the day of collection Please place your carts with the wheels facing the house so the lid opens towards the street Please place your carts at least five feet away from objects if possible (including the other cart) Please do not overload carts. If you have excess trash/recycling you must bring it to the Transfer Station Please breakdown cardboard boxes Please place shredded paper in a paper bag and staple the top closed Recycling Data Collection Summaries 2010 2010 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2011 2011 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2012 2012 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2013 2013 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2014 2014 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2015 2015 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2016 2016 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2017 2017 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2018 2018 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2019 2019 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2020 2020 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2021 2021 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2022 2022 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2023 2023 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2024 2024 Recycling Data Collection Summary 2025 2025 Recycling Data Collection Summary Pembroke Automated Collection Program Data Collection - 2026 Summary MONTH TRASH (TONS) RECYCLING (TONS) % RECYCLING RECYCLING FEE/TON RECYCLING (cost)/savings (VS. $117.93/TON FOR TRASH)* SEPTEMBER % $ OCTOBER % $ NOVEMBER % $ DECEMBER % $ TOTAL 2026 1496.84 411.25 21.63% AVERAGE $144.64 AVERAGE ($10,948.42) Eff. 9/1/25 $117.93/Ton 2026 Recycling Rates by Route MONTH MONDAY WEDNESDAY THURSDAY FRIDAY TRANSFER STATION Questions? planning_building.text: The Planning and Building Department is actively involved in all matters relating to land use, development, and preservation. The Department is located on the second floor of the Pembroke Town Hall, 311 Pembroke Street. Office hours are 8-4:30 Monday through Friday. The services and programs that the Planning and Building Department oversees include planning, economic development, building inspection, zoning and fire code inspection and enforcement, property assessing, conservation and public health. The Department, in conjunction with the Planning Board and other Town departments and boards, develops the Master Plan for the community. The Master Plan is the Town s plan and vision for the future development and growth of the Town. The Department administers the Planning Board s subdivision and site plan regulations and review process and it works with Pembroke residents and the business and development community seeking approval for various development plans that are presented to the Planning Board. fire_department.text: The Pembroke Fire Department was organized in 1869 as an on-call volunteer fire department which continues to this day. Our members are professionals dedicated to helping any of our citizens in their time of need - whether it be a fire, water problem or advice on children playing with matches. To learn more about each of us, how to contact us and who serves you please see the About Us section. For others interested in what fire equipment we have, how we are organized and our general operational setup please go to our Operations section. Not only will you see pictures of our equipment but you will also see our organizational chart and quick links to our dispatch center where you can see what is currently going on in the area. Want to join us? We welcome anyone who is, or who is perhaps, interested in joining our department to contact us or visit us. See our Training and Recruitment section for more information. Although we do not have full-time staff we can almost always be found on Tuesday evenings starting at 6:30 pm at the fire station when we get together for training each week. You can come and see what we are and we will provide you with information as needed. Preventing fires and emergencies is one of our primary goals. We have an excellent fire prevention division, which is responsible for enforcing the NH State Fire Code by conducting fire inspections and that organizes public education programs, provides guidance and information to parents and others when there might be a behavioral problem regarding fire safety, and any other help that one might need. Please see the Prevention and Education section to get more information. Burning permits can be obtained online by clicking on the Fire Permits Online link to the left. They can also be obtained, in person, during normal business hours at the Safety Center Building permits are administered by the Town Code Enforcement Officer and Building Inspector. He can be reached at Town Hall, 603-485-4747, ext. 214. link to their webpage. Our Fire Prevention Division handles existing occupancy inspections and the review of plans and inspections of fire protection systems such as fire alarm systems, sprinkler systems and fixed suppression systems. town_info.text: Pembroke s history began in 1725 when Captain John Lovewell (sometimes Lovell) and his intrepid band of Indian fighters, recruited from the towns around Dunstable, Massachusetts, decided to drive the Indians out of what is now New Hampshire. In 1728, the Honorable House of Representatives of His Majesty s Province of the Massachusetts Bay in New England granted six square miles of land to the survivors and heirs of non-survivors of Lovewell s band of Indian fighters. This land area became known as the original Suncook. On December 9, 1730, the Suncook Proprietors drew for their first division of lots, the least to contain forty acres and all others to be of equal value, regardless of the number of acres. According to the best available information, Francis Doyen, one of Lovewell s soldiers, and his wife were the first white inhabitants who ever wintered in the township, 1728-1729, and they may have been the first permanent settlers. Basically, there are three grants of land covering the same area in varying degrees. The Bow grant was granted on May 20, 1727. The Mason grant, presently known as the Masonian claim of 1621, was granted by the Council of New England established in Plymouth, County of Devon, England. The Suncook grant of August 6, 1728, was granted by His Majesty s Province of the Massachusetts Bay in New England in the General Court. The inhabitants of Buck Street and Bow, having boundaries adjacent to the Suncook boundary line, became discontented with the Township of Bow. They petitioned the New Hampshire House of Representatives to join with Suncook. In 1736, members of the Congregational church chose Reverend Aaron Whittemore to be pastor. Sometime near the period of incorporation, the Presbyterians built their own meetinghouse on a little knoll covered with a pine grove on the west side of Pembroke. The first pastor was Reverend Daniel Mitchell. Eventually, the Congregational and Presbyterian churches were reunited in Pembroke. Incorporation of Pembroke was granted on November 1, 1759, authorizing the levying and collecting such Province Tax as shall be imposed upon them by law as any other Town or Parish in this Province. On the passage of the act of incorporation, the Plantation of Suncook ceased to be, and the Town of Pembroke took her place in the fair sisterhood of the Commonwealth of New Hampshire to enjoy all the rights and privileges belonging to towns. vital_records.text: A certificate can be issued by the Town Clerk for all births, marriages, and deaths that occurred in the Town of Pembroke. A certificate can be issued by the Town Clerk for all births, marriages, and deaths that occurred in the State of New Hampshire from 1935 to present (with the exception of 1949 and 1950), marriages that occurred in the State of New Hampshire from 1960 to present, deaths that occurred in the State of New Hampshire from 1965 to present, and divorces that occurred in the State of New Hampshire from 1979 to within 6 months from the present search date. The fee is $15.00 for the search and issuance of the first certificate (the $15.00 fee will be charged whether the record is found or not) and $10.00 for each certificate issued at the same time. If processed on-line a $1.00 fee will be added. Visit the EB2Gov Payment Services site to request vital records online. assessing.text: Mission Statement: The goal of the Assessing office is to provide both a precise and efficient property tax assessment system ensuring equitable distribution of the tax burden among property owners. Duties and Responsibilities: The Assessing Department is committed to ensuring that each taxpayer receives a fair and equitable real estate assessment. This commitment involves strict adherence to state statutes governing property assessments with oversight of property exemptions, credits, and current use programs. Additionally, the department actively shares real estate information with the public encompassing property record cards, tax maps, surveys, plans, ownership records, sales data, and other pertinent information. Functions Performed by the Assessing Department Valuate all property in Town as of 1 April of the current tax year - including new subdivisions and all new construction or improvements. Maintain property values in accordance with NH Assessing Standards Board. Inspect real property on a cyclical basis to conform to 5-year certification by NH DRA. Process transfer of ownership. Process all exemption applications (Elderly, Veteran s, Disabled, Blind, Elderly/Disabled deferral). Process abatement applications. Process Intent to Cut or Excavate. Bi-annual Tax Warrants. Process current use applications or land use change tax. Defend Board of Tax and Land Appeals cases. Process yearly tax-exempt applications. Process and maintain tax map updates. Maintain property sales books. Maintain MS-1 Report to set tax rate (due September 1 each year). Maintain Sales Ratio study for the state (due November 15 each year). mercury_disposal.text: As of January 1, 2008, the State of New Hampshire law bans the disposal of mercury-containing items in the trash. Pembroke does accept the following items at the Transfer Station on Tuesday and Saturday from 7:30 am to 3:30 pm and we would be happy to recycle them for you free of charge. Fluorescent Lamps Compact Fluorescent Lamps Button Batteries Pembroke does not accept the following items at the Transfer Station. Thermometers Thermostats Tilt Switches Manometers If you have to dispose of these items please call the New Hampshire Department of Environmental Services Household Hazardous Waste Program at 603-271-2047 and they will be able to further instruct you. transfer_station_facility.text: The Town s Solid Waste Transfer Facility is located at 8 Exchange Street, adjacent to the Department of Public Works Garage. The Facility is open to residential users on Tuesdays from 7:30 am to 3:00 pm and Saturdays, from 7:30 am to 3:30 pm. Users must first obtain and display a facility permit prior to using the facility. Transfer Facility Disposal Fees Permits Facility permits are issued at the Department of Public Works. Facility permits are free of charge for Pembroke residents and allow you to utilize the Transfer Station and White Sands Conservation Area. Facility Permits expire each year on December 31st and you need to obtain a new permit each year. Please present a valid Department of Motor Vehicles Registration at the Public Works Department Office for the vehicle(s) you wish to permit. Facility permits are issued strictly to residents in the Town of Pembroke and your registration must reflect that. If your registration requires an address change you may do so free of charge at the Town Hall. The office is open Monday through Friday 8 am to 4 pm. If you have any questions please call the Public Works Department at 485-4422. Municipal parking lot permits are issued by the Police Department. solid_waste_collection.text: All household and commercial refuse generated in the Town is transported to the Casella facility located in Allenstown. The Town joined the cooperative in 1985 and signed an agreement that will provide access to the facility until the year 2009. As of January 2015 the Town has a new agreement with Casella. The Department provides curbside residential waste pickup and commercial property owners must make arrangements with a private hauler, licensed by the Town, to transport their waste. Since May 1, 2010 recycling has been mandatory in the Town of Pembroke both curbside and at the Transfer Station. Please make sure your carts are curbside by 6:45 am on the day of your collection to ensure you don t miss collection. The routes are being picked up a bit different than they were before and your trash and recycling may not be picked up at the same time it used to be. The new truck can only pick up one side of the street at a time and we are trying to find the most efficient way to plan the routes out. In addition to waste collection, residents are permitted to bring their trash and recycling items to the Solid Waste Transfer Facility. Feel free to call 603-485-4422 with questions. spring_cleanup.text: The Department of Public Works will soon be conducting its Annual Spring Cleanup for residential properties. The only items that will be picked up are bagged leaves, grass, weeds, sticks, small branches and other organic yard material in biodegradable paper yard waste bags . Brush must be no more than 4 feet in length with limbs no greater than 5 inches in diameter, and the weight of each bundle may not exceed 40 pounds. Please tie the bundles with string or light rope. Do not use wire, metal strapping or plastic rope. A maximum of one 1-ton truck load per household will be picked up. Please have your load ready at the beginning of your pickup week. Your spring cleanup week is determined by the day your curbside rubbish pickup falls on. Please note that your yard waste: Will not be picked up with the garbage truck Must be curbside by 7 am on Monday morning of your spring cleanup week. Must be in biodegradable paper yard waste bags , which can be purchased at grocery and home improvement stores (plastic bags will not be accepted for pickup) If your regular rubbish pickup is on Monday or Wednesday , your Spring Cleanup week will be the week of April 14 through April 18, 2025. If your regular rubbish pickup is on Thursday or Friday , your Spring Cleanup week will be the week of April 21 through April 25, 2025. All yard waste will picked up curbside by a separate truck. If you have in excess of one 1-ton truckload of yard waste or you miss your collection week you may bring the remainder of your yard waste to the transfer station. The Town will not make extra trips to pick up your waste if you missed the collection day. In addition, the Town will not pick up appliances, furniture, tires, etc. These items may be brought to the Town s Solid Waste Facility on Tuesday and Saturdays. There are fees for certain items. A residential Solid Waste Facility Permit is required. Agendas & Minutes Contact Us Sign Up for E-Alerts E-Reg Dog Licenses Forms & Documents

winter_parking_snow.text: Notice to All Residents On street winter parking in Pembroke is not allowed with the exception of the rules: The Town has instituted a winter parking ban from January 1st through March 31st from 12 midnight through 6 am The Director of public works also has the opportunity to at any time with notice declare a winter emergency parking ban. In the event that a parking ban is called, all notifications will be made to the news and radio stations as well as posting on the Town s website and social media sites. If a snow emergency has been called, all vehicles must be removed from the street to avoid being towed. Any vehicle not moved will be towed at the owner s expense, however, parking on the road is allowed for the following areas. Glass Street from Main to the United States Post Office. Main Street from the Allenstown Town Line bridge North to Broadway, Union Street from the Perry Eaton Building to Main Street. This is allowed so that the businesses can continue to operate. Please do not put your carts out during a snow emergency. If your trash/recycling day is on the same day as a snow emergency your collection will be on the next regularly scheduled trash day, i.e. if your pickup day is a Wednesday and a Snow Emergency is declared, your carts will be picked up on Thursday as a double route. When a Winter Snow Emergency Parking Ban is declared , please check with: WMUR Channel 9 WJYY Radio 105.5 or the Town of Pembroke s website Also, Year Round - [Amended September 5, 2017] No parking is allowed between the hours of 9 am - 2 pm on your selected trash day for the mentioned streets: Broadway to Hillcrest Central Street Church Street - From the rear exit of the bank to Main Street Front Street Glass Street - From 60 Glass Street to 129 Glass Street High Street Kimball Street Lindy Street Main Street - From Broadway to Turnpike Maple Street Millard Street Pine Street Pleasant Street Prospect Street Union Street - From High Street to 6 Union Street Agendas & Minutes Contact Us Sign Up for E-Alerts E-Reg Dog Licenses Forms & Documents

facility_permit.text: Facility Permit - for Residential Use of the Transfer Station Pembroke residents can get a Facility Permit at the Department of Public Works. Facility Permits (also sometimes referred to as a Dump Sticker ) are free. You will need to bring a valid vehicle registration showing your Pembroke address to Public Works and they will issue the Facility Permit. Public Works is open Monday through Friday 7:30 am to 3:00 pm. You can also get a permit from the Transfer Station attendant on Saturday from 7:30 am to 3:30 pm. Permits expire annually on December 31st. Please note Parking Stickers are now issued by the Police Department. If you have any questions please call the Public Works Department at 603-485-4422. The Planning Board and the Board of Selectmen will also appoint members to sit on this committee. The goal of this committee is to update and maintain the town road management plan, as well as advise the Selectmen on matters pertaining to the maintenance and construction of all town roads.
